messages:
alice: Heads up — us-west1 GPU nodepool is fully exhausted, lots of pods Pending with reason=Unschedulable. Observed sudden spike ~10m ago. Can someone triage? :warning:

ben: seeing it. cluster-autoscaler is spinning up nodes then immediately scale-down, capacity oscillation. cost alert firing.

cara: logs show a CronJob `experiment-batch` launched 480 jobs at once (parallelism=500, retries enabled). Many are `Pending` waiting for nvidia.com/gpu.

devon: who owns that CronJob? @cara which namespace?

cara: namespace=research-experiments, owner=ml-team. It was a config change from last deploy.

sre-jamie: quick mitigation: suspend the CronJob, scale its Job template to 1, and delete pending pods with label app=experiment-batch. I'll run commands unless someone beats me.

ben: go ahead. also cordon one affected node pool to stop further scheduling to noisy GKE nodes: `kubectl cordon nodepool-gpu-usw1-3`

alice: infra-bot shows many nodes in `NotReady` briefly due to NV driver init failures when new nodes boot. That maybe triggers CA to think nodes are unready and triggers more provisioning.

ops-bot: Deploy bot: `suspend` applied to CronJob/experiment-batch in research-experiments by sre-jamie at 1793123512 :white_check_mark:

devon: I'm running:```bash
kubectl -n research-experiments patch cronjob experiment-batch -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'
kubectl -n research-experiments delete pod -l app=experiment-batch --field-selector=status.phase==Pending
```

cara: after deletion, backlog dropped from 480 -> 24 pending. Autoscaler still flapping though. CA logs show fast scale-up due to pending pods, then scale-down because node group reports allocatable GPU count mismatch (driver not ready).

ben: temp fix: set CA flag `--max-node-provision-time` to 12m and `--scale-down-unneeded-time` to 10m to prevent immediate teardown. Also cap `--max-total-unready-percentage=40` so CA doesn't overreact. We'll push a safe override for the cluster.

alice: also increase node boot readiness by adding a pre-pulled nvidia driver daemonset and lowering init timeouts so new nodes don't oscillate NotReady. Devops to follow up.

sre-jamie: for immediate containment I cordoned and drained two noisy pools and tainted remaining GPU nodes with `gpu-reserved=true:NoSchedule` so only pods that tolerate get scheduled. That bought us 8 minutes of breathing room.

devon: cost note — provisional billing shows 3x spike since scale started. Finance tagged this incident. Need to tag runaway CronJob owner for chargeback.

cara: root cause: a bad merge changed CronJob `spec.concurrencyPolicy` and `spec.parallelism` on prod-like env; combined with missing resourceQuota in research-experiments allowed unlimited GPU-hungry jobs.

ben: long-term fixes: add namespace ResourceQuota limits on GPUs, set PodSpec `max-gpu` admission control, enforce CronJob sanity via CI lint (reject parallelism > 50), and add CA conservative defaults for GPU pools.

alice: action items: 1) ml-team to revert CronJob and add quota (cara) 2) infra to patch CA flags (ben) 3) platform to add admission control / CI check (devon) 4) SRE to document emergency playbook (sre-jamie). I'll create runbook PR.

ops-bot: Incident annotated: label=inc_gpu_exhaustion_1793123456, severity=high, sla-impact=true

sre-jamie: closing loop — suspending CronJob + cordon/taint + CA flag change reduced pending to single-digit and scale stabilized. Still monitoring for 30m. :mag_right:

alice: thanks everyone. follow-ups scheduled on calendar. We'll post retrospective once costs reconciled. :thumbsup:
